Generate simulated time-to-event data for two-group trials

Source: R/GenSimData.R
GenSimData.Rd

Generates Monte Carlo replicates of a two-group parallel-group trial with exponential survival times, uniform accrual, optional independent dropout, and analysis triggered when the E-th overall event is observed. Unequal allocation between treatment and control groups is supported via separate n_T and n_C arguments. Optionally, subjects are assigned to strata with their own baseline hazards, and the recorded times are rounded up to a time unit, which produces tied times.

Usage

GenSimData(
  nsim = 1000,
  n_T,
  n_C,
  hazard_C,
  HR,
  a,
  E,
  dropout_hazard = 0,
  strata_prop = NULL,
  strata_hazard = NULL,
  time_unit = 0,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

nsim

Integer. Number of Monte Carlo replicates.

n_T

Integer. Number of subjects on the treatment group (group label "T").

n_C

Integer. Number of subjects on the control group (group label "C").

hazard_C

Positive numeric. Hazard rate for the control group.

HR

Positive numeric. True hazard ratio, hazard_T = HR * hazard_C.

a

Positive numeric. Length of the accrual period; subject accrual times are drawn from Uniform(0, a).

E

Positive integer. Required total number of observed events (pooled across both groups) at which the analysis is triggered.

dropout_hazard

Non-negative numeric. Hazard rate of independent dropout. Set to 0 (default) to disable dropout.

strata_prop

Optional numeric vector of stratum probabilities (positive, summing to 1). Each subject is assigned to stratum s with probability strata_prop[s], independently of the group. Default NULL (no strata).

strata_hazard

Optional positive numeric vector of the same length as strata_prop: the hazard of a subject in stratum s is multiplied by strata_hazard[s] in both groups, so that the hazard ratio is common to all strata. Default NULL, which means 1 for every stratum.

time_unit

Non-negative numeric. If positive, the recorded times are rounded up to multiples of time_unit, which produces tied times; whether a subject has an event and the analysis time are determined from the exact times. Default 0 (no rounding).

seed

Optional integer seed for reproducibility.

Value

A data.table with one row per subject per simulation, carrying the columns simID, group (factor with levels "T" and "C"), time, and event, and, when strata_prop is given, stratum (integer stratum number). Subjects accrued after the E-th event are dropped, and subjects whose total calendar time exceeds the analysis time are administratively censored. The rows are sorted by simID and time, or by simID, stratum, and time when there are strata, so that the rows of each simulation can be passed to EstHR with is_sorted = TRUE.

Details

The data-generating process is:

  • Accrual times u_{i,j} ~ Uniform(0, a);

  • Survival times t_{i,j} ~ Exp(lambda_j) with lambda_T = HR * lambda_C;

  • Optional independent dropout d_{i,j} ~ Exp(lambda_D);

  • Analysis triggered when the E-th overall event is observed.

With strata, lambda_C is multiplied by strata_hazard[s] for the subjects of stratum s, and lambda_T by the same factor. The time and event columns (and stratum) are the variables to be passed to EstHR. Without strata_prop and with time_unit = 0, the random numbers are drawn in the same order as in earlier versions, so that a given seed gives the same data.

Examples

d <- GenSimData(nsim = 100, n_T = 100, n_C = 100,
                hazard_C = log(2) / 18, HR = 0.7,
                a = 12, E = 110, seed = 1)
head(d)
#> Key: <simID, time>
#>    simID  group        time event
#>    <int> <fctr>       <num> <int>
#> 1:     1      C 0.002155094     1
#> 2:     1      T 0.199681083     1
#> 3:     1      C 0.442931665     1
#> 4:     1      C 1.244341219     1
#> 5:     1      C 1.743443761     1
#> 6:     1      T 1.804099459     1

# Two strata with different baseline hazards, times in whole months
d2 <- GenSimData(nsim = 10, n_T = 100, n_C = 100,
                 hazard_C = log(2) / 18, HR = 0.7, a = 12, E = 110,
                 strata_prop = c(0.4, 0.6), strata_hazard = c(1, 2),
                 time_unit = 1, seed = 1)
head(d2)
#> Key: <simID, stratum, time>
#>    simID stratum  group  time event
#>    <int>   <int> <fctr> <num> <int>
#> 1:     1       1      T     2     1
#> 2:     1       1      C     2     1
#> 3:     1       1      C     2     1
#> 4:     1       1      C     3     1
#> 5:     1       1      C     3     1
#> 6:     1       1      C     3     1
